source_caption:
Rosemary Harris elevates what could have been standard comic book exposition into one of the most poignant monologues in modern blockbuster history. By speaking about the necessity of heroes and the pain of sacrificing our personal dreams, Aunt May unknowingly speaks directly to Peter Parker’s deepest internal conflict just as he has abandoned his alter ego. The brilliance of this quiet, intimate scene is how it grounds a massive superhero spectacle in pure human empathy, proving that the true emotional core of the franchise was never the breathtaking action sequences, but the quiet wisdom found in a backyard in Queens.

Spider-Man 2 (2004), directed by Sam Raimi, starring Tobey Maguire, Rosemary Harris, Alfred Molina.** A conflicted young man must balance his crumbling personal life with the heavy burden of his superhuman responsibilities when a tragic scientific accident creates a terrifying new nemesis.

source_details.title: Spider-Man 2
source_details.synopsis: Spider-Man 2 is a 2004 American superhero film directed by Sam Raimi and written by Alvin Sargent from a story conceived by Michael Chabon and the writing team of Alfred Gough and Miles Millar. Based on the Marvel Comics superhero Spider-Man, it is the second film in Raimi's Spider-Man trilogy (2002–2007), and the sequel to Spider-Man (2002). Tobey Maguire stars as Peter Parker / Spider-Man, alongside Kirsten Dunst, James Franco, Alfred Molina, Rosemary Harris, and Donna Murphy. The plot follows Peter Parker as he tries to manage his job, academics, personal life, and life as Spider-Man while also attempting to stop the scientist Dr. Otto Octavius from re-creating a dangerous experiment.
